memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: She gave this name to the Lord who spoke to her: "You are the God who sees me," for she said, "I have now seen the One who sees me." - Gen 16:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Out of her wilderness encounter, Hagar does something no one else in the Bible had done: she gives God a name. "You are the God who sees me" - El Roi. A runaway Egyptian slave becomes the first person in Scripture to name God, and the name she gives Him is about being seen. In her deepest loneliness, she discovered she was never truly alone.

Feel the wonder of her words: "I have now seen the One who sees me." Hagar had been invisible her whole life - a slave, a possession, a means to someone else's ends. No one really saw her. And then, in the desert, she discovered that the God of the universe had seen her all along. She was known. She mattered. She was seen.

This is perhaps the deepest human longing - to be truly seen and known by someone who cares. We can be surrounded by people and still feel unseen. But there is a God who sees us completely, down to our hidden pain and unspoken tears, and does not turn away.

He sees you too. Not with the cold gaze of a distant judge, but with the tender attention of a loving Father. "You have searched me, Lord, and you know me" (Ps 139:1). Jesus saw the woman at the well, the tax collector in the tree, the beggar by the road - the ones everyone else overlooked. Whatever wilderness you're in, look up. You are seen by the God who sees you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you feel unseen? How does it change things to know God sees you?
- Have you, like Hagar, come to see the One who sees you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are the God who sees me. In my loneliness and hidden pain, You have seen me all along. Thank You that I am known and loved by You. Help me live today as one who is truly seen.
Amen.
